title: Millionaire for Life: What Players Need to Know
description: Cash4Life is gone. Millionaire for Life is the new daily lifetime prize game. Here's how it works, what it pays, and how it compares.
content:
Millionaire for Life Is Now the Nation's Premier Daily Lifetime Prize Game

Effective February 22, 2026, Millionaire for Life replaced Cash4Life as the multi-state lottery game offering a lifetime annuity as its top prize. The transition was immediate — Cash4Life held its final draw on February 21, 2026, and the new game launched the very next day. As of November 3, 2026, the Millionaire for Life database has logged 254 draws, confirming the game is still in its early operational phase but drawing every single day.

The End of Cash4Life — and Why This Transition Matters

Cash4Life launched in 2014 as a joint offering among several state lotteries, including New York, New Jersey, and others. Its top prize — $1,000 a day for life — made it one of the few U.S. lottery games to offer a structured lifetime annuity rather than a lump-sum jackpot. For more than a decade, it stood as the go-to game for players who preferred steady income over a one-time windfall.

The switch to the millionaire for life lottery new game marks a meaningful upgrade in prize scale. Where Cash4Life offered $1,000 per day at the top tier, Millionaire for Life elevates that to $1,000 per day for life — valued at $7 million, with a second-tier prize of $1,000 per week for life. The lifetime structure remains, but the framing and prize architecture around it have been significantly rebuilt for a broader audience.

How Millionaire for Life Works

Draw Schedule and Ticket Price

Millionaire for Life draws are held every day of the week, consistent with Cash4Life's daily format. Tickets cost $2 per play. Players select five numbers from 1–60 and one Millionaire Ball (ML) from 1–4.

Prize Structure

  • Match 5 + ML: $1,000/day for life (top prize)
  • Match 5: $1,000/week for life (second prize)
  • Match 4 + ML: $2,500
  • Match 4: $500
  • Match 3 + ML: $100
  • Match 3: $25
  • Match 2 + ML: $10
  • Match 1 + ML: $4
  • Match 0 + ML: $3

The Millionaire Ball pool of just 1–4 gives every ticket a meaningful chance at a bonus-ball match, keeping lower-tier prizes accessible across a wide range of players.

What This Means for Players

Players who previously bought Cash4Life tickets can transition directly to Millionaire for Life at participating retailers across member states, including New York. The $2 ticket price remains the same. The key practical difference is the expanded main ball pool — Cash4Life used a 1–60 main pool with a 1–4 Cash Ball, a structure Millionaire for Life mirrors closely — making the game familiar to returning players while delivering a higher-value top prize.

The top prize of $1,000 per day for life, if structured as a 20-year minimum guarantee, equates to roughly $7.3 million before taxes. After federal and state withholding, actual annual take-home will vary by state. Use our lottery tax calculator to estimate your net prize based on your state of residence.

With 254 draws on record and the game still under a year old, the statistical picture will sharpen considerably in the months ahead.
